info.title: qscheduler
info.description:
Scheduling service dispatching tasks to quantum computing backends.

The API refers to machines, projects and notifiers by **name**. Request and response bodies are
JSON unless an endpoint says otherwise.

## Concepts

- **Machine** — a named execution target backed by a backend (`iqm` or the in-process `test`
  backend). Each machine has its own task queue and hands at most `queue_size` tasks to its
  backend at once.
- **Project** — a named, time-limited budget. Work charged to a project is rejected with
  `402` once the budget is exhausted or the project is deactivated.
- **Session** — an exclusive, time-limited reservation of one machine for one project. While a
  session is open, only its tasks run on the machine.
- **Task** — a payload forwarded to a machine's backend. A task belongs to exactly one of a
  project (it is charged its execution time) or an open session (the session's open time is
  charged instead).
- **Suspension** — a machine taken out of service with a message; new work for it is rejected
  with `409`.
- **Notifier** — a named HTTP callback target that tasks and sessions can opt into with
  `notify`.

The database is the source of truth: tasks and sessions survive a service restart, and tasks
still running on a backend are re-attached.

## Admin API

Machines and notifiers are managed through the admin endpoints (`/machines`,
`/machine/{machine}` and `/notifiers`). Changes apply to the running service at once. These
endpoints require the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token is the value of
the `ADMIN_TOKEN` environment variable of the service. When `ADMIN_TOKEN` is unset or empty,
the admin endpoints are disabled and return `403`; a missing or wrong token gets `401`. Backend
and notifier tokens are accepted but never returned.

## Notifications

A task or session with `notify` makes the service `POST` a JSON event to that notifier's URL:
for a task once it reaches a terminal state (`finished`, `failed` or `cancelled`), for a
session when it opens (`session.state` is `open`) and when it closes (`closed`). A session
cancelled before it opened only sends the `closed` event. A failed delivery is retried with
exponential backoff, up to 16 attempts.

The event body carries the same object as `GET /tasks/{id}` (`TaskInfo`) or
`GET /sessions/{id}` (`SessionInfo`), plus the notifier's token when it has one:

```json
{"event": "task", "task": {"id": 42, "state": "finished", "...": "..."}, "token": "secret"}
{"event": "session", "session": {"id": 7, "state": "open", "...": "..."}, "token": "secret"}
```

## Versioning

`info.version` is the service version and follows Semantic Versioning: a breaking API change
bumps the major version (the minor version while on `0.y.z`), any other API change bumps the
minor version (the patch version on `0.y.z`).

get.summary: Health check. Reports whether the service is up and able to reach the database.
Get a machine's configuration. The backend token is not returned.

put.summary:
Replace a machine's configuration (fields omitted from the body get their default values).
The machine is restarted with the new configuration, as on a service restart: queued tasks
and sessions are kept, tasks already handed to the backend are re-attached, and an open
session is closed (its unfinished tasks are cancelled). New tasks and sessions are rejected
with HTTP 409 while the restart is in progress.

delete.summary:
Remove a machine. Without `force`, only a machine without any tasks and sessions is
removed. With `force`, its tasks and sessions are deleted as well, and jobs already handed
to the backend get a best-effort cancel request.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description:
Remove the machine even if it has tasks or sessions; they are deleted together with
their consumption records (the consumed time is not returned to their projects).

409.description: The machine has tasks or sessions and `force` is not set

get.summary: Describe the machine's backend: its type and version information.

200.description: Backend type and version, e.g. `{"type": "iqm", "version": {"qccsw_version": "...", "server_version": "...", "station_control_version": "..."}}` or `{"type": "test", "version": "1.0"}`

500.description: Backend error, including an IQM `/about` response missing any of the version fields

get.summary: Fetch a calibration data set from the backend.

post.summary:
Suspend a machine. While suspended, the machine rejects every new task and session
(including tasks submitted into an already open session) with HTTP 409 and the suspension
message, e.g. `Machine 'garnet' is suspended: Calibration in progress`. A machine has at
most one active suspension, and it stays suspended across service restarts.
post.description:
Existing work is handled according to `cancel`, applied once when the suspension starts.
A task failed by a suspension has the error `Machine suspended: <message>`. A task already
submitted to the backend is failed right away: its cancellation on the backend is requested
(and retried while the backend is unreachable), and whatever the backend reports about it
afterwards is ignored. A project task is charged its estimated running time so far, which
never exceeds the true time.

422.description: `message` is empty or longer than 512 characters, or `cancel` is invalid

delete.summary:
End a machine's suspension; it accepts new tasks and sessions again. Work failed or closed
by the suspension stays so.

get.summary:
List a machine's suspensions, newest first. The active suspension, if any, is the first
entry and has no `resumed_at`.
List all machines, sorted by name. Backend tokens are not returned.

post.summary: Register a machine. It accepts tasks and sessions right away.

409.description: A machine with this name already exists

get.summary: List registered notifiers, sorted by name. Tokens are not returned.

post.summary:
Register a notifier — an HTTP callback target for task and session events. It can be
selected by new tasks and sessions right away.

409.description: A notifier with this name already exists

422.description: Invalid name (empty or longer than 512 characters) or URL

delete.summary:
Remove a notifier. Events already queued for it are still delivered; tasks and sessions
that use it stop sending notifications.

post.summary:
Register a project — a named, time-accounted budget that tasks and sessions are charged
against.
post.description:
A task submitted with `project` is charged its execution time; a task in a session is not
charged itself, the session's open time is. Running work counts against the budget while it
runs (checked every machine `limit_check_interval_ms`). Once the budget is exhausted, the
project's open sessions are closed, and its submitted and queued tasks end `failed` with
the error `Project time limit exceeded` (submitted ones are cancelled on the backend).

409.description: A project with this name already exists

get.summary: Get a single project by name.

patch.summary:
Update a project's `active` flag and/or time `limit_ms`. Fields omitted from the request
body are left unchanged. Does not affect `consumed_ms`.

post.summary:
Create a session — a time-bounded, exclusive reservation of one machine for one project.
The session waits in the machine's queue until it opens; while it is open, tasks are
submitted into it with `POST /tasks?session_id=…`. The project is charged the time the
session is open. Tasks in the session are cancelled when the session closes.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Name of the project the session's time is charged to.

parameters.name: time_limit_ms
parameters.description: Session lifetime in milliseconds, at most the machine's `max_session_time_ms`.

parameters.name: notify
parameters.description:
Name of the notifier to send the session's open/close events to. No notification is
sent when omitted.

402.description: The project has exceeded its time limit, or the project is not active.

409.description: The machine is suspended (the body contains the suspension message), or is being reconfigured or removed.

422.description: Unknown `project` or `notify`, or `time_limit_ms` exceeds the machine's `max_session_time_ms`.

get.summary:
Get a session's current info (state, timings, and its machine/project). Closed sessions
remain available after a service restart.

delete.summary:
Request cancellation of a session. Cancellation is asynchronous: a queued (`"waiting"`)
session is removed from the queue, while an `"open"` session is closed and its tasks are
cancelled (both those already submitted to the backend and those still queued); in both
cases the session eventually reaches the `"closed"` state.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description:
Session to associate the task with. The session must be in the `"open"` state or the
task is rejected. Exactly one of `project` / `session_id` must be given.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description:
Name of the project to charge the task's time to. Exactly one of `project` / `session_id`
must be given.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Free-form identifier of the user submitting the task, stored alongside the task.

parameters.name: time_limit_ms
parameters.description:
Maximum execution time in milliseconds, counted from when the backend starts running
the task (queue time does not count). When exceeded, the task is cancelled on the backend
and ends `failed` with the error `Task time limit exceeded`. The limit is checked every
machine `limit_check_interval_ms` against a running-time estimate that never exceeds the
true time (see the machine's `max_clock_skew_ms`), so a task is never stopped early but
may overrun slightly. Defaults to the machine's `default_task_time_limit_ms`.

parameters.name: notify
parameters.description:
Name of the notifier to send the task's completion event to. No notification is sent
when omitted.

requestBody.description: Raw task payload forwarded to the backend. For the `iqm` backend, a JSON circuit description accepted by the IQM API. For the `test` backend, a JSON object `{"outcome": {"type": "Ok"}, "result": "42", "artifacts": {"log": "..."}, "submit_time": 0.5, "compute_time": 1.5}`: `outcome` (required) is `{"type": "Ok"}` or `{"type": "Fail", "message": "..."}`; `result` (default `""`) is what `GET /tasks/{id}/result` returns; `artifacts` (default `{}`) maps names to the values `GET /tasks/{id}/artifacts/{name}` returns; `submit_time` and `compute_time` (default 0) are seconds to wait before acknowledging the submission and before reporting the result.

402.description: The project has exceeded its time limit, or the project is not active.

409.description: The machine is suspended (the body contains the suspension message), or is being reconfigured or removed.

422.description: Neither or both of `project`/`session_id` given, unknown `machine`/`project`/`notify`, `time_limit_ms` is zero, or the session is invalid or not open.

get.summary:
Get a task's current info (state, timings, and its session/project/machine/user). Finished
tasks remain available after a service restart.

delete.summary:
Request cancellation of a task. Cancellation is asynchronous: a queued task is removed from
the queue, while a running task is cancelled on the backend; in both cases the task
eventually reaches the `"cancelled"` state (poll `GET /tasks/{id}` to observe it).

409.description: Task already in a terminal state (finished, failed, or cancelled)

get.summary:
Fetch a named artifact produced for a task from the backend that ran it, forwarded
verbatim (no caching, no parsing).

200.description: Raw artifact JSON as returned by the backend

404.description: Task not found, or the backend has no artifact of this name

409.description: Task has not been submitted to a backend yet

get.summary:
Fetch a task's raw result from the backend that ran it, forwarded verbatim (no caching,
no parsing).

200.description: Raw result as returned by the backend (plain text): the full job-status JSON document for `iqm`, the payload's `result` string for `test`

409.description: Task has not been submitted to a backend yet

version.description:
For `iqm`, the version fields reported by the IQM server's `/about` endpoint; for
`test`, a plain string.

oneOf.description:
An IQM server. Task payloads must be JSON circuit descriptions accepted by the IQM API
(`POST /api/v1/jobs/{machine_name}/circuit`). A job is never given up on while the server
is unreachable or returns errors: its polls back off exponentially (from
`poll_interval_ms` up to 60 s) and return to the normal interval after the first
successful poll, and a cancel that cannot be delivered is retried on later polls. Each
request to the server times out after 10 s.

machine_name.description: Name of the target quantum device on the IQM server.

poll_interval_ms.description: Job status polling interval, in milliseconds.

token.description: Bearer token for the IQM server.

BackendRequest.description: The backend a machine dispatches its tasks to.

BackendResponse.description: A machine's backend as reported by the API (without its token).

oneOf.description: Versions reported by the IQM server's `/about` endpoint.

name.description:
Unique notifier name (at most 512 characters); tasks and sessions select the notifier
by it in their `notify` field.

token.description: Token included in every event payload.

url.description: URL to POST task completion and session open/close events to.

active.description: Whether the project can accept new tasks/sessions.

IqmVersion.description: Version fields of the IQM `GET /about` response; other keys are ignored.

MachineResponse.description: A machine's configuration; the fields mean the same as in `MachineSettings`.

oneOf.description: The active suspension, if the machine is suspended.

MachineSettings.description: A machine's configuration. Omitted fields get their default values.

default_task_time_limit_ms.description: Time limit of tasks submitted without an explicit `time_limit_ms`, in milliseconds.

limit_check_interval_ms.description:
How often session time is stored into the DB and task and project time limits are
checked for running work, in milliseconds. After a crash, up to this much session time
may go uncharged.

max_clock_skew_ms.description:
Maximum assumed lag of the backend's clock behind ours, in milliseconds. Running tasks'
time is estimated so that it never exceeds the true time while the skew stays within
this bound, so time limits never fail a task early; the estimate may lag the true time
by up to this amount (plus one poll interval), letting a task overrun its limit or its
project's budget slightly.

max_session_time_ms.description:
Maximum duration a session on this machine may request, in milliseconds. Sessions
requesting longer are rejected.

queue_size.description: Maximum number of tasks submitted to the backend at once.

NotifierInfo.description: A registered notifier as listed by the API (without its token).

has_token.description: Whether event payloads include a token.

name.description: Unique notifier name, selected by tasks and sessions with `notify`.

active.description: Whether the project can accept new tasks/sessions.

consumed_ms.description:
Confirmed time consumed so far, in milliseconds: finished tasks and checkpointed session
time, so it never decreases. Running tasks count toward the limit checks but are only
included here once they finish, with their exact execution time.

SessionInfo.description:
A snapshot of a session's public-facing data, resolved names and all — the shape returned
by `GET /sessions/{id}` and embedded in the session open/close callback.

closed_at.description: Absent unless the session has closed.

exectime_ms.description:
Milliseconds the session has been open, i.e. the time charged to its project. Updated
periodically while the session is open, so it may appear before `closed_at`.

notify.description:
Name of the notifier that receives the session's open/close events. Absent if the
session was created without `notify`, or its notifier has since been removed.

opened_at.description: Absent if the session never opened (still waiting, or closed while still queued).

project.description: Name of the project the session's time is charged to.

SessionStateKind.description: The current state of a session, as a plain string (no embedded data).

SuspendCancel.description: What happens to a machine's existing work when it is suspended.

message.description:
Why the machine is suspended (at most 512 characters). Returned in the error of every
rejected task/session submission, and in the error of every task failed by `cancel`.

Suspension.description: A machine suspension — the active one, or a past one from the history.

resumed_at.description: Absent while the suspension is still active.

TaskInfo.description:
A snapshot of a task's public-facing data, resolved names and all — the shape returned by
`GET /tasks/{id}` and embedded in the task completion callback.

backend_id.description: Backend-assigned job ID. Absent until the task is submitted to the backend.

exectime_ms.description: Milliseconds of execution time consumed, if any.

finished_at.description:
When the task reached its final state; absent while it is `waiting` or `running`. For a
task that ran on the backend, this is the backend's timestamp (`finished_at - started_at`
equals `exectime_ms`); for a task ended by the scheduler itself (e.g. cancelled while
queued), it is the scheduler's time.

notify.description:
Name of the notifier that receives the task's completion event. Absent if the task was
submitted without `notify`, or its notifier has since been removed.

project.description:
Name of the project the task's time is charged to, if it was project-parented directly
(not via a session). Mutually exclusive with `session`.

session.description: Session the task ran in, if it was session-parented. Mutually exclusive with `project`.

started_at.description: When the backend started running the task, on the backend's clock. Absent until then.

time_limit_ms.description:
Execution time limit in milliseconds, counted from `started_at`. When exceeded, the task
is cancelled on the backend and ends `failed`. Absent only for tasks created before time
limits existed.

user.description: Free-form identifier of the user who submitted the task.

TaskStateKind.description: The current state of a task, as a plain string (no embedded data).

active.description: Whether the project can accept new tasks/sessions. Omit to leave unchanged.

limit_ms.description: Time budget, in milliseconds. Omit to leave unchanged.
